plate_findings.evidence: Calcifications in head of pancreas, absent pancreas body and tail

panels.rationale: Whole-figure plate of 8 panels (A, B, C, D, E, F, G, H). A: CT image showing renal cysts and calcifications, consistent with HNF1B related kidney disease. B: CT image showing pancreatic calcifications and hypoplasia/absence of pancreatic body and tail, a classic HNF1B manifestation. C: H&E-stained renal biopsy section showing tubular damage with microcalculus, supporting nephrocalcinosis associated with the HNF1B diagnosis. D: Polarized light microscopy confirming the presence of oxalate microcalculus in renal tissue, correlating with nephrocalcinosis. E: CT scan showing the absence of the pancreatic body and tail, a diagnostic feature of HNF1B related pancreatic hypoplasia. F: CT image demonstrating complicated pancreatic head pathology (cysts and calculi) alongside renal calculi, associated with HNF1B. G: CT scan demonstrating pancreatic agenesis of the tail and bilateral renal involvement (cysts and calculi), consistent with HNF1B. H: CT scan showing bilateral renal cysts and...

in_text_mentions: for at least 25 years, presented in April 2012 with progressive kidney dysfunction. Despite excellent glycemic control on insulin, her kidney function deteriorated significantly over several months. A kidney biopsy revealed mesangial expansion, consistent with diabetic nephropathy, alongside intratubular calcium oxalate depositions, which raised suspicion for hyperoxaluria (Figures 2C, D, III-1). The patients' family history was remarkable for kidney disease affecting her father and sister, suggesting an underlying genetic kidney disease. Three cousins had been diagnosed with cystic fibrosis.

tudies, showed high urine oxalate (178 mg/dl, normal range <40 mg/dl) and low urine citrate (<28 mg/dl) while genetic testing for AGXT variants, associated with primary hyperoxaluria type 1 (PH1), returned negative. CT abdomen and pelvis revealed calcifications in the pancreatic head, atrophy or agenesis of the pancreatic body and tail, and multiple kidney stones and kidney cysts (Figures 2A, B, III-1). The persistence of high urinary oxalate level and pancreatic calcifications and partial agenesis on imaging suggested secondary hyperoxaluria due to malabsorption from pancreatic insufficiency.

Her initial lab results showed mild liver enzyme elevations (AST 65 IU/ml, alkaline phosphatase 170IU/ml) with normal kidney function, electrolytes, and pancreatic enzymes. CT abdomen showed a possible mass in the pancreatic head, along with calcifications in the pancreatic head and hypoplasia of the body and tail and multiple kidney stones (Figures 2E, F, III-2), Follow-up MRI abdomen and MRCP showed that she was missing the body and tail of her pancreas. Pancreatic enzyme replacement was started to help with exocrine insufficiency.

plate_findings.evidence: The patient has multiple cysts in the right kidney

panels.rationale: Whole-figure plate of 2 panels (A, B). A: Abdominal ultrasound shows a human patient (right kidney) with multiple renal cysts, which is a clinical manifestation of HNF1B related kidney disease, specifically renal cystic dysplasia. B: Abdominal ultrasound shows a human patient (left kidney) with multiple renal cysts, which is a clinical manifestation of HNF1B related kidney disease, specifically renal cystic dysplasia.
